mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding 3 months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, thereby producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of quarters where this trigger is met, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 4.5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative in at least 70% of triggered instances, or the median return is not below the 5th percentile of historical returns.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (CPI) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a monetary policy tightening coinciding with rising inflation, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both above 12-month moving average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not below the 10th percentile of historical returns.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly decline in both real personal income (proxied by RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 1% signals a broad-based weakening in household demand, which reduces economic activity and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and HOUST both decline by > 1% month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the average return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 0.5% month-over-month for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not above the 50th percentile of historical returns.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized GDP growth (GDPC1) below 1% for two consecutive quarters signals economic stagnation, which reduces corporate profit growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of other conditions.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative in at least 70% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not below the 25th percentile of historical returns.
